Devin Park: Quick sync — designing the calibration + prompt sets for the FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ bakeoff. Do we go strict stratified splits or a hierarchical/adaptive holdout? @Laura any prefs? :thinking_face:
Laura Chen: I lean hierarchical. First stratify by domain (docs, conversations, code, math), then by difficulty band inside each domain. That gives both coverage and targeted stress tests. :+1:
Miguel Torres: How big are we thinking? 12k total OK? maybe 70/20/10 for train/calib/holdout per-domain? worried about edge-case sparsity.
Sarah Patel: Also need prompt variation templates + paraphrase augmentation for calibration so quant artifacts don't overfit one phrasing. Include multi-turn and format-preserving tests (tables, json).
Devin Park: Agree on templates. Proposal sketch: 1) Domain stratify -> 2) Difficulty bins (easy/med/hard) -> 3) Per-bin sample budget with oversample of rare labels -> 4) Small curated adversarial control (manual). Example sampling snippet:```python
def sample(bucket, target_n, seed=42):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    core = rng.choice(bucket.core, size=int(target_n*0.8), replace=False)
    tail = rng.choice(bucket.tail, size=target_n-len(core), replace=True)
    return np.concatenate([core, tail])
```
Laura Chen: Metrics we should capture on calibration & holdout: EM/F1 where applicable, calibration delta (prob->empirical), hallucination rate (fnr on fact queries), token-level perplexity shift, and prompt-sensitivity (std of outputs over paraphrases).
Miguel Torres: For quant bakeoffs include k-fold style rotating holdouts so each model sees the same held-out distribution. Seed tracking + exact prompt hashes are critical for reproducibility (seed=42 everywhere).
quant-bot: calib-set-gen finished — size=12350 examples; domains: docs(48%), convo(22%), code(18%), math(12%). Uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/calib/1839991234.tar.gz :package:
Sarah Patel: For the curated adversarial control I can take 500 items and do manual review next week. Will annotate with failure-mode tags (format-break, long-context, ambiguity, numeric-precision). :hammer_and_wrench:
Devin Park: Nice. Next steps: Laura to produce per-domain bin definitions + sampling script, Miguel to wire k-fold runner and seeding, Sarah to produce the 500 adversarial items. I'll schedule a 30m sync after artifacts land. Marking owners here: @Laura, @Miguel, @Sarah :calendar: :eyes:
